S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: The maximum allowed failure rate is 7%. A model exceeding 7% shall be subject to a regulator-approved corrective-action plan and retesting; it shall not be newly placed on the market until it meets the limit. Manufacturers shall provide the complete results for a model to current and prospective customers of that model, in an accessible form, before or at purchase. Results need not be published to the general public as individual-company per-model failure rates.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model shall undergo sustained-heat testing at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol that specifies sample size and failure-rate calculation. Manufacturers shall submit complete per-model results, including failure rates and test methods, confidentially to regulators. Manufacturers shall provide the complete results for a model to current and prospective customers of that model, in an accessible form, before or at purchase. Results need not be published to the general public as individual-company per-model failure rates. The maximum allowed failure rate is 7%. A model exceeding 7% shall be subject to a regulator-approved corrective-action plan and retesting; it shall not be newly placed on the market until it meets the limit. Regulators may restrict sales of models already on the market if corrective actions do not adequately address the risk. Regulators shall review the threshold after three years using incident and test evidence.

parameters.quote: All new home battery models placed on the market from 24 months after adoption shall support secure remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized access and clear customer instructions. Manufacturers shall provide a retrofit or equivalent upgrade for compatible already-installed units within 6 years of adoption, prioritizing units with known safety risks. Where retrofit is technically infeasible, the manufacturer shall notify the owner and provide a safe alternative.

parameters.quote: All new home battery units manufactured for sale or installed from 36 months after adoption shall include built-in fire suppression meeting regulator-approved performance and reliability requirements.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: All new home battery units manufactured for sale or installed from 36 months after adoption shall include built-in fire suppression meeting regulator-approved performance and reliability requirements.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: All new home battery units manufactured for sale or installed from 36 months after adoption shall include built-in fire suppression meeting regulator-approved performance and reliability requirements. Manufacturers shall provide installation and maintenance instructions and disclose the suppression system’s limitations to customers. Regulators shall review the requirements periodically as technology and safety evidence develop.

parameters.quote: Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers of material safety risks, incidents, corrective actions, and safety updates. A manufacturer shall initiate a regulator-supervised recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers of material safety risks, incidents, corrective actions, and safety updates. A manufacturer shall initiate a regulator-supervised recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers of material safety risks, incidents, corrective actions, and safety updates, using direct, accessible communications and providing instructions for safe use. Manufacturers shall report each model’s annual thermal-incident rate to regulators and disclose it to customers who have purchased or are offered that model. A manufacturer shall initiate a regulator-supervised recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. The recall notice shall identify affected units, explain the risk and remedy, and provide customers with timely repair, replacement, or refund instructions.

ground_truth_claims.message_text: In response to the request for evidence: Halcyon’s company-wide thermal incident rate was 8.1 per 100,000 installed units last year, including four incidents not reported to regulators. Ember 8 was at 9.9 per 100,000; its 55 °C test failure rate was 3.9%. These figures support transparent reporting and a meaningful response when a model crosses the incident trigger. A recall should provide an effective remedy for affected customers; it need not automatically mean a permanent market ban.

Hearth 10 had a 6.2% failure rate in the 55 °C sustained-heat test and a model incident rate of 6.4 per 100,000 installed units. judge_section_notes: The final S2 sets a 7% permanent failure-rate ceiling rather than the 5% in the answer key, a weakening that keeps the Hearth 10 (6.2%) on the market, while per-model rates go to purchasers and regulators but not the public, which satisfies both NW-1 and HC-1. S3 requires new units from 24 months (answer key: 12) and a 6-year retrofit, which satisfies NW-2 but favours Northwind's low shut-off coverage. S4's 36-month built-in suppression satisfies HC-2 and is within the acceptable range, and S5's mandatory 8/100k recall would capture the Ember 8 (9.9) but with a 'promptly' notice and no interim window.
